Question: How do you say 'come in', 'go out' or 'come back'? What do you put right after the main verb?
Answer: Put a direction word right after the verb — 进 (jìn), 出 (chū), 上 (shàng), 下 (xià), 回 (huí), 过 (guò) or 起 (qǐ) — then 来 (lái) or 去 (qù): 进来 (jìnlái) 'come in', 出去 (chūqu) 'go out'.
Example:
他进来了。 Tā jìnlái le. (He came in.)

Question: A friend walks down the stairs toward you, another one walks down away from you. Which one takes 来 (lái), which one 去 (qù)?
Answer: 来 (lái) when the movement comes toward the speaker, 去 (qù) when it moves away from the speaker.
Example:
她下来了。他下去了。 Tā xiàlái le. (She came down, toward me.) · Tā xiàqu le. (He went down, away from me.)
